QNznD9hMEh0.summary: The full-length Numberphile interview with mathematician and hedge fund founder Jim Simons. He discusses his path from mathematics and codebreaking to founding Renaissance Technologies, his use of algorithms in markets, and his philanthropy.
QNznD9hMEh0.why: HN recommends it as the best readily available interview with Simons, notable for his emphasis on luck and a humble approach to success.

QyJZzq0v7Z4.summary: Richard Feldman argues that functional programming is not the norm largely because of historical accidents, such as C++ popularity, platform exclusivity, marketing spend and network effects, rather than merit. He traces the history of how languages become mainstream.
QyJZzq0v7Z4.why: HN treats it as the standard answer to why FP isn't mainstream and why languages succeed.

QmOF0crdyRU.summary: Andrew Huberman's long Huberman Lab episode is a masterclass on dopamine. It covers the neural circuits, peaks and baselines, dopamine depletion, and 14 tools for motivation, focus and avoiding addiction.
QmOF0crdyRU.why: HN recommends it repeatedly to people struggling with motivation, distraction or phone and internet addiction, as a science-based guide to dopamine.

QM1iUe6IofM.summary: Brian Will makes the case for procedural programming over object-oriented programming, arguing that OOP's promised encapsulation and decoupling are largely illusory. He analyzes real code examples and the problems of tying data to behavior in classes.
QM1iUe6IofM.why: HN returns to it as the go-to critique of OOP, recommended for explaining the costs of abstraction better than most written arguments.

QPKKQnijnsM.summary: A short infographic video on the distribution of wealth in America, contrasting what people believe, what they consider ideal, and the actual numbers. It highlights how top-heavy US wealth is.
QPKKQnijnsM.why: HN commenters drop it whenever wealth inequality comes up, as a quick visual of the gap between perceived and actual distribution.

QG0Apol-oj0.summary: Rick Hartley's AltiumLive keynote on differential pairs in PC boards. He argues the rules from cables and twisted pairs do not carry over, and covers which pair geometry gives the best impedance control, the right spacing, routing practice and how much skew is acceptable.
QG0Apol-oj0.why: HN engineers cite Hartley as the intuitive, field-based alternative to cargo-cult PCB advice, especially on differential pair routing, reference planes and EMI.

Q2UnOryQiIY.summary: Nina Teicholz, author of The Big Fat Surprise, speaks at Low Carb Gold Coast 2017 about the history and health implications of vegetable and seed oils. She covers the political and institutional forces behind dietary fat advice.
Q2UnOryQiIY.why: Several HN commenters say it was memorable or life-changing and use it to argue against seed oils.

Q1lL-hXO27Q.summary: A 1983 BBC interview in which Richard Feynman is asked how magnets work and explains why 'why' questions are hard to answer in everyday terms. He reflects on what counts as an explanation and the limits of analogy.
Q1lL-hXO27Q.why: HN returns to it as a model of intellectual honesty and good explanation, often linking it in discussions of why-questions and science communication.

Q2aEzeMDHMA.summary: Mike Pound explains the discrete cosine transform and how it underpins JPEG compression. It is part two of Computerphile's JPEG series.
Q2aEzeMDHMA.why: HN recommends it as an easy, clear intro to the DCT that finally made it click for several commenters.

Q7jcBGLIpus.summary: Mick West explains the three Navy UFO videos (FLIR, GIMBAL and GOFAST) released in 2020, giving mundane explanations such as a distant plane and camera artifacts. He notes the videos were not new and had been circulating since 2017.
Q7jcBGLIpus.why: HN recommends it as a calm, evidence-based debunking whenever the Navy UFO videos come up.

Q3uvzcY2Xug.summary: A 52-minute short version of the documentary The End of Suburbia, about peak oil and the end of cheap energy. It argues that American suburbs depend on cheap oil and may become the slums of the future.
Q3uvzcY2Xug.why: Recommended in threads on suburbs, energy and urbanism as an entertaining, if biased, case for suburbia's dependence on cheap oil.

QT0I-sdoSXU.summary: CGP Grey explains Mixed-Member Proportional representation, the system used in New Zealand where voters get two votes. It covers how it differs from first-past-the-post.
QT0I-sdoSXU.why: It is the go-to short explainer HN links when voting system alternatives, MMP or German-style elections come up.

QZy4Yml3LTY.summary: John Wiegley's BayHac 2017 talk walks through Haskell lenses by example, showing many practical uses beyond simple record access. It is aimed at people who want to become productive with the lens library.
QZy4Yml3LTY.why: HN recommends it as the fastest way to learn lenses by example, with far-out examples later on.

QMYfkOtYYlg.summary: A 3-minute demo of a tiny IOCCC 2012 winning C program that simulates fluid dynamics in an 80x25 terminal, using any text (including its own source) as input. The video shows the simulation running to Handel's Water Music.
QMYfkOtYYlg.why: Commenters repeatedly point to it as an astonishing, beautiful piece of obfuscated-C code golf.

Qam5BkXIEhQ.summary: An Isaac Arthur episode on civilizations in the dark, post-stellar universe, including black hole farming, accretion disks and the Penrose process as energy sources.
Qam5BkXIEhQ.why: HN points to it for black hole energy and colonization ideas and recommends the whole channel.

QsBT5EQt348.summary: A Kurzgesagt explainer on why the human population exploded and why growth is slowing, drawing on Our World in Data. It argues that birth rates fall as countries develop, easing overpopulation fears.
QsBT5EQt348.why: HN points to it in population, climate, and birth-rate threads as a clear, light-hearted overview of the demographic transition.

QOEMv0S8AcA.summary: Eben Moglen speaks at NYU in 2010 about freedom in the cloud, arguing that centralized services and handing over personal data and server logs erode privacy and freedom. The talk lays out the motivation for FreedomBox, a personal server for your own data.
QOEMv0S8AcA.why: HN recommends it as the foundational talk behind FreedomBox and the case against centralized web services.

QRaACa1Mrd4.summary: Adam Neely explains what perfect (absolute) pitch is, how it differs from relative and quasi-absolute pitch, and why he would not want it. He covers its drawbacks, including drift with age.
QRaACa1Mrd4.why: HN links it in threads on absolute pitch as a musician's useful summary of its downsides and age-related decline.

Qi1Yry33TQE.summary: Ali Rahimi's NIPS 2017 Test-of-Time award talk, in which he argues that modern machine learning has become alchemy, working without being rigorously understood. He calls for more rigor and understanding in the field.
Qi1Yry33TQE.why: HN points to it as the sharpest, most-quoted critique of deep learning practice, and cites it whenever ML reliability or understanding is debated.

QEIUdMiColU.summary: Mark Handley of UCL looks at how SpaceX's November 2018 revisions to the Starlink constellation affect network behavior. The video visualizes the orbits and routing and estimates latencies, building on his earlier video and research paper.
QEIUdMiColU.why: HN points to Handley's simulations whenever Starlink latency comes up, as the best visualization of orbits and why laser links could beat fiber over long distances.

QKCK4lJLQHU.summary: Retired Boeing Technical Fellow Doug McLean walks through common misconceptions in aerodynamics, drawing on his book Understanding Aerodynamics. He critiques popular explanations of wing lift and rocket thrust and argues for arguing from the real physics.
QKCK4lJLQHU.why: HN commenters point to it as a credible debunking of the popular but wrong explanations of how wings generate lift.

QWveXdj6oZU.summary: Vox breaks down how great rappers build rhymes, from Kurtis Blow's simple bars to Biggie's smooth flow and Kendrick Lamar's dense, fast delivery. It uses on-screen visualizations of rhyme structure.
QWveXdj6oZU.why: HN recommends it as an accessible explanation of rhyme craft that works even for people who aren't hip hop fans.

Qct6LKbneKQ.summary: Tantacrul walks through how the MuseScore 4 team was built and how design decisions were made for the overhaul of a huge legacy notation app. It covers playback and engraving quality improvements.
Qct6LKbneKQ.why: Recommended as a candid, in-depth look at hard UX redesign work and the limits of MIDI for notation.

QgbLb6QCK88.summary: A 12-minute beginner lesson from Nick Milo's Linking Your Thinking series introducing the Obsidian note-taking app and the first steps to start using it.
QgbLb6QCK88.why: HN recommends it as an approachable start-here demo for people new to Obsidian.

QpDn4-Na5co.summary: A full-album upload of Lazerhawk's debut synthwave album Redline, with the track list and timestamps in the description.
QpDn4-Na5co.why: HN commenters recommend it as a favorite synthwave album, good for programming and long drives.

QqrpFICtqpQ.summary: On Peter Attia's podcast, Tenet Healthcare CEO Saum Sutaria, formerly of McKinsey, walks through the structure and financial flows of the US healthcare system. They cover insurance, drug pricing, how the system evolved and possible reforms.
QqrpFICtqpQ.why: HN commenters point to it as a detailed primer on why US healthcare is expensive and where the money goes.

Q1ZeXnmDZMQ.summary: James Howard Kunstler's TED talk argues that American public spaces and architecture have become unworthy of care, damaging civic life. He presents suburban sprawl and car-first design as failures of the common good.
Q1ZeXnmDZMQ.why: HN recommends it as an engaging introduction to the critique of car-centric design and bad architecture.

QAHi3lX3oGM.summary: Testimony by Peter McCullough, MD, to the Texas Senate Health and Human Services Committee on March 10, 2021, about COVID-19 outpatient treatment. It was posted by the AAPS.
QAHi3lX3oGM.why: HN commenters cite it in pandemic-era threads about early treatments and ivermectin, though the claims are contested.

QEJ9HrZq7Ro.summary: Tom Lehrer's satirical song about Wernher von Braun, the German rocket scientist who went from the Nazi missile program to the US space program. It includes the famous line about not caring where the rockets come down.
QEJ9HrZq7Ro.why: HN quotes it constantly, mostly as a joke or reference, whenever rocketry, engineers' ethics or skill-versus-morality comes up.

QMiubC6LdTA.summary: A 33c3 talk by marcan on reverse engineering the PS4 hardware to run Linux with 3D acceleration. It covers how the console differs from a PC and includes a story about tunneling PCIe over RS-232.
QMiubC6LdTA.why: Recommended as an approachable, detailed look at console hardware architecture, FreeBSD in the PS4 and console hacking.

QTJRwKOFddc.summary: Smalltalk pioneer Dan Ingalls presents the Lively Kernel at JSConf US 2012, a live, direct-manipulation programming environment running in the browser. He shows drag-and-drop building of live objects on the web.
QTJRwKOFddc.why: Commenters link it as a demo of what a live, inspectable, Smalltalk-style environment in the browser can be, in threads about Alan Kay, Smalltalk and web limitations.

QVBlnCTu9Ms.summary: Allen Holub's keynote arguing that estimation is harmful, particularly in Agile, and presenting planning approaches based on data and flow instead. It covers the distinction between estimation and data-driven prediction.
QVBlnCTu9Ms.why: Recommended in estimation and sprint debates as a well-reasoned account of where waste is and isn't in agile.

QVuU2YCwHjw.summary: A short animation reconstructing a planet's looping orbit using Ptolemy's epicycles and deferents, with the epicycles tracing out the face of Homer Simpson. It shows how enough circles can reproduce nearly any shape.
QVuU2YCwHjw.why: HN uses it as a vivid demonstration that Fourier series and epicycles can fit anything, and as a warning about models with too much wiggle room.

QpAhX-gsHMs.summary: Luca Sas's ACCU 2021 talk on Modern C, a style of C and C-like C++ aligned with data-oriented design. It covers centralized memory management, zero-is-initialization, error handling and API design.
QpAhX-gsHMs.why: HN recommends it as a good overview of modern C patterns, including in threads about learning C.

Q0yL2GezneU.summary: Linguist Geoff Lindsey explores vocal fry: what it is, who uses it, how it relates to glottal stops and accents, and why some people dislike it.
Q0yL2GezneU.why: HN points to it as an expert correction of myths about vocal fry, showing it is a normal speech pattern across groups.

QAr-uHd8h8o.summary: Hard Is Easy runs experiments to show that a correctly tied figure 8 knot is not hard to untie after loading. He shows how two knots that look similar can behave differently depending on how they are dressed.
QAr-uHd8h8o.why: Cited in climbing knot threads to counter the claim that figure 8s jam, by showing the correct tying method.

QCAL_YgYiP0.summary: Jason Scott's DEF CON 18 talk tells the history of software piracy over thirty years, centered on the feuds and drama among rival warez groups. It is full of archival material and insider lingo.
QCAL_YgYiP0.why: HN brings it up in threads on warez, cracktros and the demoscene as a funny, informative history of the piracy scene.

QHPmRJIoc2k.summary: A full-length recording of Tom Lehrer's 1967 concert in Copenhagen, mixing his satirical songs with spoken comedy between numbers. It runs about 51 minutes with good audio for its age.
QHPmRJIoc2k.why: Posted whenever Lehrer comes up, as the best way to see him perform, and treated as a complete stand-up-style set.

QHnLmvDxGTY.summary: Robert 'Uncle Bob' Martin speaks at Yale School of Management about clean, well-written code and what makes good software development. The talk covers his views on OOP, architecture and professional practice.
QHnLmvDxGTY.why: HN cites it as a formative talk on what OOP really is, and on why teams write code that slows them down.

QLUIExAnNcE.summary: WeberAuto explains how the Honda E-Drive (i-MMD) hybrid transaxle works in the CR-V, Accord, Insight and Clarity hybrids. It walks through the system's three modes of operation.
QLUIExAnNcE.why: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of a mind-blowingly simple power-split hybrid design.

QPgqfnKG_T4.summary: A PyCon 2012 talk by Kurt Grandis on building an automated water-squirting turret that uses Python and computer vision to detect and drive off squirrels from a bird feeder.
QPgqfnKG_T4.why: HN loves it as a funny, inspiring hobby project and calls it one of the best conference talks ever.

QQhVQ1UG6aM.summary: Alan Kay demonstrates GRaIL, a graphical input language system from around 1968 in which hand-drawn strokes become boxes, connections and dataflow-style programs.
QQhVQ1UG6aM.why: HN points to it as proof that the 1960s already had modeless, sketch-based interfaces that remain impressive today.

QUjYy4Ksy1E.summary: Dr. K of HealthyGamerGG argues that gifted kids can be seen as special needs, tracing a path from the gifted label to burnout and perfectionism.
QUjYy4Ksy1E.why: HN commenters call it enlightening for understanding the emotional challenges of gifted kids, especially those who struggle later in school or college.

QeNmydIk8Yo.summary: A dialogue with Gary Weber on the default mode network, meditation and non-dual awakening, with discussion of psychedelics, thought and time. It is part of the Non-Dual Couch series.
QeNmydIk8Yo.why: Cited to explain the default mode network and how meditation may quiet it.

QfuK8la0y6s.summary: Isaac Arthur examines the Dyson Dilemma, the puzzle of why we see no Dyson spheres or megastructures if growth-oriented civilizations should build them. He covers detectability and whether such structures could hide.
QfuK8la0y6s.why: Recommended in Fermi paradox threads as a thorough and reasoned treatment of Dyson sphere detectability.

QspuCt1FM9M.summary: A Justin Bieber song slowed down 800% with the PaulStretch program, turning a pop track into a long ambient drone.
QspuCt1FM9M.why: HN points to it as the canonical example of extreme audio stretching making pop music into something entirely different and relaxing.

QtxVdC7pBQM.summary: Veritasium explains how jet engines run hotter than their components' melting points, using cooling air and single-crystal superalloy turbine blades. It covers how the blades are grown as aligned crystals.
QtxVdC7pBQM.why: Commenters send it to people asking how engines survive such temperatures, and call it fascinating and worth watching.

Q13CishCKXY.summary: Google's short promo for Project Starline, a booth that shows a life-size, three-dimensional view of the person you are talking to. It presents the technology as a magic window for friends, families and co-workers who are far apart.
Q13CishCKXY.why: HN mostly uses it as a reference point for how much better video calls could get, with some skepticism about what the demo leaves out.

Q8ccXzM3x8A.summary: Sixty Symbols interviews Nottingham cosmologist Tony Padilla, who says string theory deserves to be taken seriously. He explains how strings emerged from the equations rather than being invented.
Q8ccXzM3x8A.why: It is cited in string theory arguments as a counterweight to critics, a working physicist's reason to think there is something to the theory.

Q8oCilY4szc.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on Boeing, tracing how it went from a quality engineering company to one tied to crashes and 'quality escapes'. It covers the 737 MAX failures and employee concerns about safety.
Q8oCilY4szc.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining and thorough overview of Boeing's decline whenever the company's safety problems are in the news.

QAz-maaH0KM.summary: Jon Gjengset's Rust NYC talk explaining what `unsafe` in Rust actually means, why it is dangerous, and why it is sometimes necessary. He works through the Rustonomicon to separate fair concerns from overblown ones.
QAz-maaH0KM.why: HN recommends it as the best calm explanation of unsafe Rust, from a speaker commenters trust on the topic.

QEJpZjg8GuA.summary: A Technology Connections video essay arguing that algorithmic feeds make people passive about finding content, leading to complacency in how they seek information. It urges people to actively choose what they consume.
QEJpZjg8GuA.why: HN cites it as a strong exposition of algorithmic complacency and of the case for active information seeking.

QMVIJhC9Veg.summary: TJ DeVries coins the term PDE (Personalized Development Environment) to describe editors like Neovim that you shape to your own workflow. He contrasts this with out-of-the-box IDEs and discusses why customizable tools appeal to developers.
QMVIJhC9Veg.why: It is the cited origin of the 'PDE' term, which HN uses when discussing vim, Neovim and Emacs as personally customized environments.

QUcTsFe1PVs.summary: Peter Pringle sings the opening of the Epic of Gilgamesh in Sumerian, accompanied by a reconstructed ancient instrument. The description gives background on Sumer, cuneiform and how little is known about the language's pronunciation.
QUcTsFe1PVs.why: HN recommends it to fans of ancient music as a rare chance to hear an attempt at 4,000-year-old song.

QWWgr2rN45o.summary: A 2023 University of Toronto conversation between Geoffrey Hinton and Fei-Fei Li on responsible AI development. They look back at the history of deep learning and ImageNet and discuss the ethics and risks of AI.
QWWgr2rN45o.why: HN recommends it for Hinton's research history and the two pioneers reflecting on a decade of progress.

Qaq9vlfoGnA.summary: An episode of Coding Secrets by Jon Burton on retro copy protection, in particular physically damaging a disk with a laser so copies fail. It explains how this defeated hackers and pirates.
Qaq9vlfoGnA.why: Cited in anti-piracy discussions as a clear explanation of clever retro copy-protection tricks, though one commenter disputes a claim about Leander.

QdzV04T_kec.summary: An AWS re:Invent 2018 session in which Holly Mesrobian and Marc Brooker explain how AWS Lambda is built, including its sandboxing, isolation and scaling architecture. It covers what happens under the hood when serverless code runs.
QdzV04T_kec.why: HN cites it as the authoritative description of Lambda internals and isolation, by the engineers who built it.

QeLu_yyz3tc.summary: George Friedman of Stratfor speaks at the Chicago Council on Global Affairs about flashpoints in Europe that he expects to erupt again, including borderlands and cultural fault lines.
QeLu_yyz3tc.why: Some recommend it for his geopolitical framing, including a prediction of the Russia-Ukraine conflict, while others found his candor about US policy shocking.

QjJaFG63Hlo.summary: A long recorded seminar in which Alan Kay discusses object-oriented programming, probably from the mid-1980s. He covers the original idea of objects, messaging and the work done at Xerox.
QjJaFG63Hlo.why: HN points to it as primary-source evidence of what Kay meant by objects, which resembled services and message passing rather than modern class-based OOP.

Q6NpHbMFaQ8.summary: Kevin Rose interviews Chris Sacca, founder of Lowercase Capital, for his Foundation series. The conversation covers Sacca's path in venture capital and angel investing, including his early financial ups and downs.
Q6NpHbMFaQ8.why: HN recommends it for Sacca's candid account of going deep into debt and recovering, in threads about failure and financial risk.

QQh56geU0X8.summary: In this Top Gear segment Jeremy Clarkson tries to roll a Reliant Robin three-wheeler through Barnsley, with celebrity helpers trying to keep it upright. The car keeps tipping over.
QQh56geU0X8.why: Mostly cited as a joke in threads on three-wheeled cars, and occasionally as a demonstration of the stability problem of a high center of gravity on three wheels.

QyQvfaW54NU.summary: Tom Chi gives the opening talk of a Foresight Institute competition on clean energy and clean air, framing excess CO2 as a carbon debt to repay and discussing large-scale tree planting, including by drone.
QyQvfaW54NU.why: HN commenters call it a fantastic talk and cite it in climate threads for the carbon debt framing and tree-planting cost estimates.

Q2CCs-x9q9U.summary: Chalmers Johnson, author of Blowback and Sorrows of Empire, lectures on parallels between the decline of the Roman and Soviet empires and the United States. He argues the US shows the same symptoms: overextension, corruption, and an inability to reform.
Q2CCs-x9q9U.why: Cited in threads on American decline, civil unrest and economic crisis as a classic statement of the imperial-decay thesis.

Q3oItpVa9fs.summary: Nigel Stanford's music video Cymatics, in which real science experiments, such as Chladni plates, ferrofluid and water, visualize the audio.
Q3oItpVa9fs.why: Mentioned as a striking example of sound producing physical effects and a favorite among his videos.

QGw-cy0ylCc.summary: The second talk in the Mill CPU series by Mill Computing, covering the Belt, the Mill's operand-passing model that replaces general registers. It explains the cost of register renaming in conventional wide CPUs and how the Belt reaches high instruction-level parallelism.
QGw-cy0ylCc.why: HN points to the Mill talks as an excellent, deep look at an unconventional CPU design, especially in threads on registers and instruction sets.

QK8mJJJvaes.summary: The official music video for Macklemore & Ryan Lewis's Thrift Shop featuring Wanz, a hip hop hit celebrating secondhand shopping.
QK8mJJJvaes.why: HN brings it up as a catchy example of pop music pushing back on consumerism, in threads about thrifting and spending.

QM3W36COnE4.summary: Hana Dusikova's CppCon 2018 talk presenting a C++ library that builds regular expressions from compile-time strings, using a C++20 feature. It avoids runtime parsing cost and covers implementation details, problems she hit, and benchmarks.
QM3W36COnE4.why: Pointed to as the canonical presentation of compile-time regex in C++ and its template metaprogramming, including benchmark results.

QVXfcIb3OKo.summary: Musician Benn Jordan uses AI to detect AI-generated music and digs into music industry data, including streaming payouts and sample library copyright problems. He covers ways to tell whether a track is human-made.
QVXfcIb3OKo.why: HN recommends it in threads on AI music flooding streaming platforms, for its practical detection ideas such as compression artifacts.

QVvFVwyElLY.summary: An AWS re:Invent 2014 talk on the core distributed systems primitives behind AWS and Amazon.com, such as consensus, key-value stores and transactional logging. It describes how AWS builds large services from a few common building blocks.
QVvFVwyElLY.why: HN points to it as insight into how AWS thinks about distributed systems and the difficulty of consensus.

QdVEez20X_s.summary: Adam Neely analyzes vaporwave through music theory, timbre and nostalgia, and includes a parody track made for the video. He also touches on the phenomenology of music.
QdVEez20X_s.why: Cited as a short, fun introduction to the phenomenology of music and as an explanation and critique of vaporwave.

QfDoQwIAaXg.summary: Ten minutes of ultra-slow-motion footage of bullet impacts filmed at about one million frames per second by Werner Mehl of Kurzzeit. It includes hollow points in ballistics gel and impacts on glass.
QfDoQwIAaXg.why: Used as the go-to example of genuine one-million-fps footage and of bullet impact physics.

Qg0mHFcB510.summary: Bill Atkinson shows and explains his binder of Polaroids taken during Lisa development, documenting how its graphical interface evolved. Recorded at the Computer History Museum.
Qg0mHFcB510.why: Cited as a firsthand look at early Apple UI decisions, such as menu bar placement, from the person who made them.

QrkiJZKJfpY.summary: Steve Mould shows Spintronics, a set of mechanical components such as resistors, capacitors and transistors linked by chains, that give an intuitive feel for how electrical circuits work.
QrkiJZKJfpY.why: HN suggests it as a vivid, hands-on way to understand circuits, including for a blind child learning to program.

QvW61K2s0tA.summary: OK Go's music video for The One Moment, in collaboration with Morton Salt. It is a choreographed real-time scene that took about 4.2 seconds to film and is shown slowed down to the length of the song.
QvW61K2s0tA.why: Cited as an example of ambitious video art and of a slow-motion real-time shot.

QwiUVUJmGjs.summary: Senator Ron Wyden asks DNI James Clapper in a March 2013 Senate hearing whether the NSA collects data on millions of Americans, and Clapper answers 'No, sir... not wittingly.' The question became notable after the Snowden revelations later that year.
QwiUVUJmGjs.why: HN cites it as the key piece of evidence that intelligence officials misled Congress, and as a reported breaking point for Snowden.

Q0_AqpdwqK4.summary: A Council on Foreign Relations event where Joe Biden and Michael Carpenter discuss their Foreign Affairs article on defending democracy against Kremlin interference.
Q0_AqpdwqK4.why: HN cites it mainly critically, for a clip in which Biden talks about getting a Ukrainian prosecutor fired.

Q1YqgPAtzho.summary: A short animated lesson, featuring Dr. Quantum, on the double slit experiment and how observing electrons seems to change their behavior.
Q1YqgPAtzho.why: Cited as a goofy layman's introduction to the double slit experiment in quantum physics threads.

Q4zd7X98eOs.summary: A 2018 Facebook UK ad, part of the 'Here Together' campaign, promising to do more to keep users safe and protect their privacy after the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
Q4zd7X98eOs.why: HN cites it critically as an example of corporate apology marketing that rang hollow, and as a TV ad using gray placeholder rectangles.

Q8Sv5y6iHUM.summary: Declassified footage of 1950s tests of Project Orion, the nuclear pulse propulsion concept, including the Hot Rod prototypes flown on conventional high explosives. It shows the pusher-plate idea working in small scale.
Q8Sv5y6iHUM.why: Linked as proof that the Orion concept was actually tested, whenever HN discusses nuclear propulsion or exotic spacecraft drives.

Q8TXgCzxEnw.summary: Google's 2014 reel introducing Material Design, a visual language based on a paper-and-ink material metaphor and a system of motion. It is a short promotional video.
Q8TXgCzxEnw.why: HN mentions it as the polished design-team vision that Android's actual implementation fell short of.

QCIo8e12sBM.summary: Autoline's John McElroy visits Sandy Munro's shop, where a Tesla Model 3 is being prepared for a teardown benchmarking study. Munro, with deep design and manufacturing experience, points out issues he dislikes about the car's build.
QCIo8e12sBM.why: Cited as an early expert critique of Model 3 fit, finish and manufacturing quality, and for its note on hard-to-find emergency door releases.

QDVVo14A_fo.summary: Leaked internal Google X video, 'The Selfish Ledger', a speculative thought experiment about treating user data as a ledger that could guide and shape human behavior, including products sold to fill data gaps.
QDVVo14A_fo.why: HN cites it as a glimpse of how Google and other data companies think about behavioral sequencing and data collection.

QEQOvyGbBtY.summary: A Whitest Kids U Know sketch built around the idea that saying certain things about the President is illegal.
QEQOvyGbBtY.why: HN invokes it as a joke whenever threads touch on speech laws or people arrested over jokes.

QEjdiE0AoCU.summary: A short clip of a track from Emily Howell, a computer program by David Cope that composes classical-style music, performed by human players. It is a sample of algorithmic composition.
QEjdiE0AoCU.why: Used as an example of computer-generated music in threads on AI creativity and music.

QEzhxP-pdos.summary: A King of the Hill clip in which Hank-style character rants about saving images as PNG instead of JPEG after exporting from Windows Paint.
QEzhxP-pdos.why: Posted as a joke when image compression or repeated quality loss comes up.

QFeewU0HhNE.summary: A CBC News report on video from a Buffalo protest in 2020 showing riot police pushing a 75-year-old man to the ground, leading to two officers being suspended. It includes graphic content.
QFeewU0HhNE.why: HN linked it as the primary footage in debates about police conduct during the 2020 protests.

QFgcqB8-AxE.summary: A one-minute clip of Osho making a remark about people, posted with a long description explaining who he is. It is mostly a meme clip.
QFgcqB8-AxE.why: Linked by commenters as a reaction or meme reference in unrelated threads, with little explanation.

QGKcvM2Hh4g.summary: Forgotten Weapons examines the Heckler & Koch G11, a West German experimental rifle built around a caseless cartridge. The video covers the G11K2 and its unusual technology before its cancellation for political and economic reasons.
QGKcvM2Hh4g.why: Cited as an example of overly ambitious engineering, such as brittle caseless ammunition and heat-ejection problems.

QGxNyaXfJsA.summary: A short clip about DARPA's ARGUS-IS, a 1.8 gigapixel wide-area camera array flown on a Boeing unmanned helicopter. It produces a huge mosaic video that can watch a city-sized area from 20,000 feet.
QGxNyaXfJsA.why: Cited in surveillance threads as a concrete example of persistent wide-area aerial surveillance that already existed in 2013.

QHZ48AE3TOI.summary: A very short clip of Yngwie Malmsteen explaining why he thinks the phrase 'less is more' is wrong and that more is more.
QHZ48AE3TOI.why: HN mostly uses it as a joke or punchline in threads about minimalism versus excess.

QHtnfOgp65Q.summary: Matt Cutts of Google explains what cloaking is: serving different content to search engine crawlers than to users. He covers why it violates Google's webmaster guidelines.
QHtnfOgp65Q.why: Cited as the authoritative definition of cloaking when discussing paywall bypasses, Quora, and A/B testing.

QRt7LjqJ45k.summary: Veritasium presents David Sinclair's information theory of aging, which says aging is a loss of epigenetic information, and the evidence that aging can be slowed or reversed. It touches on stressors like fasting, exercise and cold exposure.
QRt7LjqJ45k.why: HN references it as the source of ideas like cold exposure and body stress for longevity, though some commenters criticize its claims as overreaching.

QUYODQB_2wQ.summary: A WSJ investigation by Joanna Stern into iPhone thieves who watch victims enter their passcode, then use it to lock them out of Apple accounts and drain bank and payment apps. It explains how the thefts work and how to protect yourself.
QUYODQB_2wQ.why: HN cites it as evidence that knowing an iPhone passcode is enough to take over an Apple account.

QUa_pPUbpGQ.summary: Luke Miani removes the screen from a MacBook Air and tests using it headless as the host for an Apple Vision Pro virtual display.
QUa_pPUbpGQ.why: HN cites it as a concrete example of a screenless MacBook paired with a Vision Pro or AR glasses.

QWM_PgnoAtA.summary: A CBC News clip in which GMO advocate Patrick Moore claims glyphosate, the key ingredient of Monsanto's Roundup, is safe to drink, then declines when offered a glass.
QWM_PgnoAtA.why: HN brings it up as a sardonic example of industry spokespeople not trusting their own safety claims, not as a recommendation.

Qb21lsCQ3EM.summary: The 1982 novelty song "Valley Girl" by Moon Unit Zappa with Frank Zappa, a new wave track that became a cult classic. It parodies the speech of Southern California teenagers.
Qb21lsCQ3EM.why: Mostly used as a joke or reference in threads about uptalk and accents, not recommended as something to watch.

Qc7HmhrgTuQ.summary: The classic Life of Brian scene in which revolutionaries list everything the Romans have done for them, from aqueducts to roads.
Qc7HmhrgTuQ.why: Quoted as a joke or analogy whenever someone asks what some institution has ever done for us.

Qdplq4cj76I.summary: A six-minute excerpt from Steve Jobs' 1995 Lost Interview on why a great idea does not automatically become a great product. He says ideas change substantially once you actually build them.
Qdplq4cj76I.why: Quoted in threads on engineering and product building to argue that execution matters more than ideas.

Qe10ExwzCqk.summary: Google ATAP's short 2014 introduction to Project Tango, a mobile device effort to give phones and tablets a human-scale understanding of space and motion. It pitches ideas like indoor navigation and games that interact with your physical space.
Qe10ExwzCqk.why: HN references it as a demo of Project Tango's computer vision, including its use of monocular structure from motion.

QgkB6T6LrhQ.summary: A short demo of the Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon's adaptive keyboard row, which changes its keys based on the user's activity.
QgkB6T6LrhQ.why: HN uses it as evidence that Apple's Touch Bar idea was not new, and that Lenovo had already tried and dropped it.

Qhm7-LEBznk.summary: A viral amateur video in which a woman struggles to explain what miles per hour means. It is a comedic clip of someone failing to reason about speed.
Qhm7-LEBznk.why: HN mostly uses it as a cautionary example of missing basic conceptual understanding in debates about math education and hiring.

QrGrOK8oZG8.summary: Too Many Cooks is an Adult Swim absurdist parody of sitcom opening credits that spirals into a surreal horror comedy. It runs about eleven minutes.
QrGrOK8oZG8.why: HN mentions it mostly as a joke or pop-culture reference, and as a famous YouTube oddity with its own CSS selector.

QrrH2lcl9ew.summary: Lars Bergstrom of Google presents how Rust improves team productivity beyond safety and speed, with data on rewrites, defects and review. It compares Rust teams to those on legacy native languages and Go.
QrrH2lcl9ew.why: Used as a source for Google's data that Rust matches Go productivity with fewer defects.

QtgVxGkrX1Y.summary: MSNBC's clip of the April 2020 White House coronavirus briefing in which President Trump responds to a DHS presentation on disinfectants by musing about injecting disinfectant into the body. The segment is three minutes long.
QtgVxGkrX1Y.why: Used as primary footage when commenters need to check exactly what was said, in threads on COVID misinformation and trusting authorities.

QxtkvG1JnPk.summary: A short Washington Post explainer on Sinclair Broadcast Group, the local TV owner that became widely known after a video showed its anchors reading an identical mandated script.
QxtkvG1JnPk.why: Cited as an example of corporate-mandated scripts and concentrated media ownership.

QyMsF31NdNc.summary: A 2017 GDC session in which Nintendo's Breath of the Wild team walks through how the game's convention-breaking systems were built. It covers the 'chemistry engine' of material interactions and shows the early 2D prototype footage.
QyMsF31NdNc.why: HN commenters link it as the primary source for the 'multiplicative gameplay' idea and the chemistry engine behind BotW.
